c.tagline: A slender coral necklace of a capital, ringing an impossibly blue lagoon.

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis run the length of the main road for a small flat fare (about $0.75-1); private/negotiated hire costs more, especially at night or out to Laura.

emergency.police: 625-8666 (Majuro Police HQ; there is no nationwide 911-style number)
emergency.medical: 625-3355 / 625-4144 (Majuro Hospital, Ministry of Health & Human Services)
emergency.note: Ambulance coverage is very limited and slow; for urgent injuries a taxi to Majuro Hospital in Delap is often faster.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: Majuro's compact commercial core along Uliga Road, with the main shops, banks, dive/boat operators and the flagship Hotel Robert Reimers clustered together; suits travelers who want walkable convenience.
The lagoon-side government district holding the Capitol (Nitijela), ministries and the atoll's largest resort; suits business travelers and anyone wanting waterfront sunset views close to services.
The denser, more residential eastern end of the Delap-Uliga-Djarrit strip running out to Rita; quieter and more local, suiting budget travelers and longer-stay visitors.
A 45-minute drive west past the airport to the widest white-sand beach on the atoll and a laid-back village feel; suits beach lovers and anyone wanting a rural escape.
Private lagoon islets reachable only by boat, from a simple family-run cottage to an ultra-exclusive private-island retreat; suits honeymooners, divers and travelers chasing total seclusion.

water.note: Tap water is not safe to drink due to bacterial contamination risk; use bottled water.

sys.n: Marshall Islands Shipping Corporation Field-Trip Ships

transit.pay: There is no fare card or app; visitors pay cash in USD directly to the driver. Shared taxis (functioning as the de facto bus system) charge a small flat per-ride fee along the main road, while private hire is negotiated on the spot. Inter-atoll ferry tickets are bought directly from the shipping company office in Delap.
transit.hours: Shared taxis run informally roughly 6am-11pm with no fixed timetable; there is no night service after that aside from pre-arranged private rides.
transit.note: Majuro has no rail or formal bus network - getting around the narrow atoll strip relies on shared taxis, private taxis, walking, or bicycles.

bus: No formal public bus network; shared taxis serve this role along the main road
ferry: Marshall Islands Shipping Corporation inter-atoll field-trip ships

airport.name: Marshall Islands International Airport (Amata Kabua Int'l, MAJ)
rentals: RRE Rent-a-Car (Robert Reimers Enterprises, arranged through Hotel Robert Reimers)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in the Marshall Islands; it's neither expected nor practiced at most restaurants, hotels, or taxis.
